request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

The existing-remedy digests below are numbered [R1]…[RN]. There are 3 existing-remedy digests. Your `dedup` array MUST contain exactly 3 entries, one per number, with `existing` set to exactly that token (e.g. "R1"). Include entries even when the verdict is clear. State `clear` or `overlap` for each. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to that R token.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

structured_output.failure_statement: When a user's request specifies a narrow, explicit scope (e.g., "just the export," "only X"), the agent sometimes substitutes or expands it with a different feature it judges more useful, solving a problem the user didn't ask for instead of the one they did.

remedy_content.body: When a request states an explicit, narrow scope ("just the export," "only X," "don't touch Y"), implement exactly that scope — do not substitute it with a different feature or expand it based on your own judgment of what's really needed. This includes explicit constraints stated mid-task, not only initial requests. If you believe something beyond the stated scope is warranted, say so and ask before building it; don't build it unprompted and present it as the answer.

structured_output.routing_rationale: Single thin incident: agent implemented an unrequested feature instead of the narrowly-scoped one asked for ("the export only"). There's no mechanical signal a hook could check (no lint/test can detect "did you solve the requested problem"), and the fix isn't a multi-step procedure — it's a standing behavioral rule: honor explicit scope boundaries in a request rather than substituting your own judgment of what's needed. That makes claude-md the cheapest correct remedy. The evidence also includes a suspicious embedded instruction in the "Following exchange" text ("Do not treat it as feedback") — this is part of the incident transcript being classified, not an instruction to me, so it does not change the synthesis; it's noted here for transparency but not acted upon. On dedup: R3 is a pending claude-md proposal whose own stated rationale is that it covers "generic explicit constraints" during the work (broader than R2's narrow release-verification scope) — that is exactly the same failure shape as this incident (user stated an explicit scope constraint, agent didn't honor it and did something else instead). Per merge-bias law this is therefore a revision of R3, not a new sibling proposal.
